title: Hierarchical rate-bucket with persistent ledger checkpoints for reserved-capacity resets
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Reserved capacity customers and high-priority tenants experience correctness issues during quota reset windows (daily/monthly and rolling epochs). Edge cases observed: clock skew during cutovers, mid-cycle tenant migrations between pools, overlapping reset windows for cross-region tenants, and bursts that should be charged against reserved vs hosted buckets. Existing reset implementations are centralized and stall on large migrations, producing stale usage ledgers and temporary overage exposures.

Proposal: Implement a hierarchical token-bucket model backed by a small persistent checkpointed ledger. Each tenant gets a top-level reserved bucket and one or more priority sub-buckets (real-time, background, burst). Checkpoints of bucket state are written atomically at configurable intervals and at reset boundaries. On reset, the system performs an idempotent checkpoint swap: new buckets are instantiated locally from a shadow ledger entry and the old checkpoints are archived for audit and billing reconciliation. This design aims for:
- Strong correctness guarantees (idempotent resets, deterministic reconciliation)
- Low-latency path for issuance and checks (in-memory token buckets with background persistence)
- Fast recovery during migrations via checkpoint replay instead of global rollbacks

Key design trade-offs considered:
- Frequency of persistence: more frequent checkpoints reduce lost-op windows but increase write load. We propose a hybrid approach: local in-memory delta aggregation with periodic durable checkpoints (default every 15s) and synchronous checkpointing only at reset gates and migration handoffs.
- Storage backend: prefer existing durable metadata store (Postgres leader-follower with write-ahead-logs) to avoid introducing a new distributed system. Use lightweight fencing tokens (etcd lease IDs) to avoid concurrent reset races.
- Complexity vs compatibility: the new API preserves existing quota tokens semantics for hosted customers; reserved pools opt into hierarchical buckets via a feature flag.

Deliverables: design doc, prototype in quota-service, migration tool to backfill archived checkpoints, telemetry and billing reconciliation jobs, canary rollout and rollback procedures.
acceptance_criteria: All reset operations are idempotent and tested against simulated duplicate-delivery and retry scenarios
No more than 1% of tenants experience transient overage windows during migration in synthetic 200k-tenant load test
Checkpoints persisted within 15s under normal load and within 200ms of a reset gate event
Billing reconciliation can replay archived checkpoints to reconstruct usage for any tenant within 72 hours
Feature flag to enable hierarchical buckets per-reserved-pool and ability to fall back to legacy reset behavior
updates: 2026-02-28: Ticket created after SRE incident where a cross-region migration caused a 3-hour billing mismatch (root cause: global reset stall)
2026-03-01: Architectural review with infra and billing teams; agreed on hybrid checkpoint cadence and Postgres-based ledger prototype
2026-03-02: Prototype implemented in quota-service: in-memory token buckets + async checkpoint writer. Local unit tests for idempotency added.

2026-03-03: Load simulation run (200k tenants, mixed reserved/hosted). Results: 99th percentile reset swap latency 120ms; mean checkpoint write latency 38ms under synthetic I/O. Observed write amplification during heavy migrations; next steps to introduce backpressure and batched writes.
2026-03-04: PM requested additional telemetry for per-tenant billing delta and an integration test with billing-reconcile job. Added to scope.
2026-03-05: Design review feedback applied: make migration handoff synchronous with checkpoint fence token; add idempotency keys; prepare canary plan
comments: Marco Nguyen: Prototype PR available at https://github.com/redwood-inference/quota-service/pull/412 — needs bench harness and more unit tests for concurrent reset scenarios
Leah Kim (SRE): Please ensure runbooks updated; recommend alert when checkpoint write latency > 500ms for >30s
Omar Rodriguez (Billing): Add reconciliation hook to replay archived checkpoints into billing pipeline; expect minor schema change to billing OLAP feed
Priya Desai (PM): Approve feature-flag approach. Request rollout telemetry on per-tenant cost delta during canary
Code review note: Make sure ledger records include reset boundary timestamp (UTC) and tenant timezone tag for auditability
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): 1% of reserved pools, feature flag on, monitor checkpoint.latency and billing.delta for 48h
Phase 2 (expanded): 10% reserved pools, add migration handoff tests, run nightly reconciliation and compare results to legacy system
Phase 3 (full): opt-in default for all new reserved pools, migrate existing pools gradually in low-traffic windows
Fallback: server-side feature flag to route specific tenants back to legacy reset implementation; telemetry to detect divergence
rollback_plan: Flip feature flag off for affected pools — this must be fast and idempotent
If feature flag flip fails or divergence persists, pause new resets and run a manual ledger reconciliation job using archived checkpoints
Notify billing and customer-facing teams and open incident if >0.5% tenants show billing delta > $500 in trial canary
implementation_notes: Data model: ledger rows keyed by tenant_id + epoch_id + priority_bucket, include fence_token and seq_no
API: PUT /v1/quotas/{tenant}/checkpoint with idempotency_key; return swap_token on success
Migration: backfill tool reads legacy accumulators and emits synthetic checkpoints into archived table; reconciliation job compares archived vs live checkpoints
Testing: add chaos tests for clock skew, duplicate-delivery, and simultaneous migration + reset; include property tests for idempotency
Ops: add alert when billing.reconcile job produces >0.1% mismatches during canary
